name: 2021 freelance-platform due-diligence evasion model

attribution.legal_posture: UN Panel reporting; some claims reproduce Member State information and remain outside criminal adjudication.

caveats: One observed account generated only about $1,050 over a year; this is an account-level amount rather than a network-wide estimate.
The Panel did not identify the platform or publish the sensitive identity details retained in this finding.

statements: The Panel reported use of false identification, VPNs and Hong Kong front companies to evade platform due diligence and know-your-customer checks.
Most linked accounts in one company investigation operated from China; accounts often moved customers off-platform after contact and targeted platforms with weaker security or due diligence.

A Jilin-linked account was connected to four additional accounts through a Chinese phone number and IP addresses and used likely fraudulent identity data; the Panel warned of unintentional platform access to international payment systems.

sources.support: Supports false-ID/VPN/Hong Kong-front methods, China operating location, off-platform migration and lower-control platform targeting
